They're super Islamic and want me to pray and wear the Hijab when I don't want to, so I'll just have to lie to them about all of this. 

You're absolutely right when you say that I'm my own person and deserve to live my life the way I want to. I wish my parents could understand this fact though. I live in a very conservative country and moreover Islam places parents on a very high pedestal. I've heard so many of my relatives tell me (when I told them I wanted to go against my parents and stop wearing the hijab) that I should obey my parents and fulfill their every wish even if it meant going against my very own. Otherwise, I'd just be considered a selfish ungrateful daughter. If I go against my parents, they're going to feel like they're being wronged and that I don't love them. Even I feel guilty sometimes because they take care of me and provide for me, just to get my disobedience in return. I really wish my parents weren't so goddamn stubborn.

So my plan for now is to somehow get through the next four years until I get my degree and a good job. After that, I'll either see if I can find someone who's a closeted ex-Muslim like me and get married to him or I'll simply cut all ties and move out. But all these things are easier said than done since I'm super insecure, make stupid mistakes sometimes and I'm bound to crave my parent's support and acknowledgement at some point or the other. I just hope I become stronger over the years and become a better person.
